subject: Culture
title: Public Shaming Rituals
description: A 60-second lesson on Public Shaming Rituals.

hook.text: In colonial America, a man caught lying spent a day locked in a wooden pillory while neighbors threw rotten food.

buildup.text: Public shaming predates prisons. Stocks, pillories, and scarlet letters turned the community into judge and jury.

discovery.text: China's 'struggle sessions' during the Cultural Revolution forced accused elites into public self-criticism.

twist.text: Western nations abolished physical shaming. Then Twitter reinvented it without the legal safeguards.

climax.text: Jon Ronson documented how a single tweet destroyed careers the same way a pillory destroyed reputations.

punchline.text: The pillory went digital and lost its time limit.

quiz.question: Who wrote about modern public shaming's resemblance to historical punishment?
